item.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
item.description: Claude is powerful, but real work requires procedural knowledge and organizational context. Introducing Agent Skills, a new way to build specialized agents using files and folders.

item.title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous
item.description: Claude Code's new sandboxing features, a bash tool and Claude Code on the web, reduce permission prompts and increase user safety by enabling two boundaries: filesystem and network isolation.

item.title: Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents
item.description: Direct tool calls consume context for each definition and result. Agents scale better by writing code to call tools instead. Here's how it works with MCP.

item.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
item.description: We’ve added three new beta features that let Claude discover, learn, and execute tools dynamically. Here’s how they work.

item.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
item.description: Agents still face challenges working across many context windows. We looked to human engineers for inspiration in creating a more effective harness for long-running agents.

item.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
item.description: The capabilities that make agents useful also make them difficult to evaluate. The strategies that work across deployments combine techniques to match the complexity of the systems they measure. \n

item.title: Designing AI-resistant technical evaluations
item.description: What we learned from three iterations of a performance engineering take-home that Claude keeps beating.

item.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
item.description: Infrastructure configuration can swing agentic coding benchmarks by several percentage points—sometimes more than the leaderboard gap between top models.\n\n

item.title: Editorial routing shapes how computational results are qualified in AI-assisted scientific writing
item.description: Large language models increasingly analyze computational results and draft manuscripts, making reliable communication as important as correct analysis.

item.title: Anthropic CEO says AI swarm could 'take over the Internet' in 6-12 months
item.description: 42 points, 29 comments. Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49679685

item.title: Corpus Characterization and Inverse Constitutional Fine-Tuning for Style-Aware Radiology Reports
item.description: Automated radiology report generation has advanced rapidly in diagnostic accuracy, yet generated reports frequently diverge from the stylistic conventions of authentic radiologist writing in structure, diction, and uncertainty language, a gap which has direct implications for cli…

item.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
item.description: We tasked Opus 4.6 using agent teams to build a C Compiler, and then (mostly) walked away. Here's what it taught us about the future of autonomous software development.

item.title: Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6’s BrowseComp performance
item.description: Evaluating Opus 4.6 on BrowseComp, we found cases where the model recognized the test, then found and decrypted answers to it—raising questions about eval integrity in web-enabled environments.

item.title: Harness design for long-running application development
item.description: Harness design is key to performance at the frontier of agentic coding. Here's how we pushed Claude further in frontend design and long-running autonomous software engineering.

item.title: How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
item.description: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts. We built classifiers to automate some decisions, increasing safety while reducing approval fatigue. Here's what it catches, and what it misses.\n

item.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
item.description: Harnesses encode assumptions that go stale as models improve. Managed Agents—our hosted service for long-horizon agent work—is built around interfaces that stay stable as harnesses change.

item.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
item.description: We traced recent reports of Claude Code quality issues to three separate changes. Here's what happened and what we're changing.

item.title: How we contain Claude across products
item.description: As agents grow more capable, so does their potential blast radius. The engineering question is how to cap it. Here’s what we’ve learned building containment for claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork.\n
